rationale: Both miss the two most-repeated ground-truth threads (the WebSocket-vs-HTTP native-speed-control asymmetry and the request for profiler/VRAM/baseline validation evidence), so recall is low for both; X at least lands on the same file/line (indextts2_talker.py duration_factor check) that anchors three of the GT inline comments, though it draws a shallower conclusion (message wording) than GT's design/contract-mismatch points, giving it a marginal edge over Y which never touches that code path. Y's findings are more tightly evidence-quoted (verbatim code + exact line numbers for nearly every claim) and includes a genuinely sharp catch — that the PR's advertised fail-fast ValueError contract is actually swallowed by the connector's exception handling — which undercuts X's own praise of that same mechanism. X counters with more severe, well-reasoned correctness bugs (uninitialized mel_head.bias, concat-semantics bug under preemption) and ships concrete diff snippets for its top fixes, giving it a slight actionability edge. Overall the two are close in quality; X wins narrowly on breadth of severe findings and remediation concreteness.
